frames.review_note: Minor issue: the silver chain of office is drawn as a heavy linked chain with a medallion. In 1.2 and 1.4 it is a thin beaded strand, so the chain is inconsistent across the page. Everything else matches the script and the bible. The fort courtyard is laterite with tiled roofs, the squall comes off the sea over the far wall, and the men are dragging oiled cloth over the barrels. The plan board in the mud has only map-like lines and no lettering. Nagoji has the topknot, grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin with light shading, the gold ear stud and a cream mundu and shoulder cloth. He has no knife, no bandages and no coat. The dark sky across the top centre and top left leaves room for both captions.

Minor issues: the chain is a thin beaded silver strand, not the heavy chain from 1.1, though it matches 1.4. Nagoji is bent at the low doorway with one arm on the jamb, peering in, rather than already partway through it, which still reads as ducking in. Everything else is right. The shoulder cloth hangs loosely over his head as a hood, not tied, and the topknot shows beneath it. Rain sheets off the eaves and the room ahead is dark. His face matches the sheet, with the moustache, a clean chin, the ear stud and grey at the temples. The hands are sound and there is no painted text. The sky at top left leaves room for the caption.

Acceptable. Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin face, receding hairline with curly side hair, plain white cloth, no chain. He sits cross-legged at a low table with a stylus, looking up calmly, framed by the door posts. The clay tags carry only abstract dots and bars, and the oil lamp is a brass bowl with an open wick. Minor: no visible ink stains on his fingers. For the RAMAYYAN balloon, use the plain grey wall beside the high window, upper centre and right (about x 0.60-0.68, y 0.05-0.30), or over the upper shelves. If panel 4 is regenerated, match this panel's very low table, unbarred slit window and brass bowl lamp.

Minor issues: Nagoji's chain is the thin beaded strand, matching 1.2 but not 1.1. Ramayyan's ink-stained fingertips are dark at the nails and read slightly like painted nails. The screen direction is correct. Nagoji is wet, just inside the door at frame left, with water dripping into a pool on the floor. His face matches the sheet, with the topknot, moustache, clean chin, ear stud and the scar on his left forearm. Ramayyan sits cross-legged at frame right at the low table with the lamp, lifting his hand toward the shelves. He matches his sheet: a thin face, receding hairline, plain white cloth and no chain. The clay tags are blank. The plain dark wall above and between the two men leaves room for all three speech lines.

Minor only. Nagoji matches the ch21 look: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with skin texture only, gold ear stud, cream mundu with shoulder cloth, silver chain, no knife, coat or bandages. He moves along the same lamp-lit archive aisle with its barred rain window. His left palm rests on the shelf bundles, though the script says he turns sideways so he will not brush them. It still reads as him moving through the shelves. The foreground clay tags carry slot and dot tally marks, which count as abstract marks. Lettering space: the low-detail grey wall left of his face (about x 0.40-0.62, y 0.15-0.45) for NAGOJI, and the top-left or bottom-left corner over the tags and bundles for the CAPTION.

Minor acting deviation. Ramayyan looks down at the bundle, where the script says he does not look at his hands. The beat still reads: he sits at frame right and pulls the string loose with practised ease. He matches his sheet: thin face, receding hairline with curly sides, plain white cloth, ink-stained fingers, no chain. The lamp, low table and barred rain window match the room in 2.1 and 2.5. Lettering space: the plain wall and window shaft at top centre (about x 0.25-0.48, y 0.0-0.4) for the first line, and the shelves at top left for the second.

Minor. The insert shows hands only and no faces. The lamp-lit leaf is held flat and square to camera and has exactly four empty bands with no marks, so the four LEAF lines can be lettered straight onto them. The ink-stained thumb sits in the left binding margin beside the second band rather than the first. It does not cover any band. The leaf fills about 82 percent of the frame width. The hands are anatomically sound and the white sleeves match Ramayyan's cloth.

Acceptable with minor notes. Hands only, no faces, no painted text or marks (the leaf and clay tags are blank), no anachronism. The ink-stained left thumb rests at the left edge beside the lower band, next to the string holes, and has clearly moved down from its 2.3 position. Both hands are anatomically sound, with white cloth at the wrists as in 2.3. The leaf shows two clear empty bands with only thin edge strips above and below. Minor: the framing is a little wider than 2.3, the window has no bars, and the lamp table sits further down the aisle instead of directly below the leaf. It still reads as the same room and the same lamp-lit leaf. Lettering guide (LEAF lines go on the bands, not in boxes and with no tails): line 0 in the upper band, about y 0.215 to 0.36, x 0.10 to 0.86. Line 1 in the lower band, about y 0.365 to 0.51, x 0.17 to 0.86, starting right of the left thumb. Keep clear of the right thumb at about x 0.87, y 0.33 to 0.39.

Minor only. The screen direction is right: Nagoji stands at frame left mid-cough with his fist at his mouth, and Ramayyan sits calm at frame right, watching him. Both match their sheets and the ch21 row: topknot, grey temples, curled moustache, ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, no knife, coat or bandages. There is faint stubble shading at Nagoji's jaw. The brand on his raised left forearm is drawn as a small, fairly crisp spoked wheel near the elbow rather than a blurred puckered patch near the wrist. It has no letters and no cross, and the white scar sits beside it. Ramayyan holds a closed bundle and a stylus in his lap rather than an open leaf. Lettering space: the dark wall and window area at upper centre and right (about x 0.52-0.82, y 0.0-0.33) and the shelves at top right for both RAMAYYAN lines, and the shelves at top centre-left beside Nagoji's head for NAGOJI.

Minor only. The leaf fills about two-thirds of the frame width, not the full width. The white cloth at top right is Ramayyan's shoulder and reads a little like a draped bundle. Otherwise clean: the ghosted Padmini bleeds in at the left with a stain-like edge and matches her sheet (coiled black hair, gold stud and necklace, cream sari with gold border, no blouse, walking stick). The leaf has empty ruled bands for both LEAF lines, the ink-stained fingers sit at the right edge, the clay tags carry only faint abstract marks, and there is dark table space at the bottom for the caption.

Minor only. The index fingertip rests just inside the leaf's left end and overlaps the first part of the upper band rather than sitting purely in the margin, so both LEAF lines should start at about x=0.19. Both bands are clean and empty from about x=0.19 to x=0.81, after which the indigo stain starts. A thin unruled strip runs along the top edge, but the two ruled bands read clearly. The clay tags carry only faint abstract scratches, not script. The hand anatomy (left hand, palm down: index, partial middle finger, thumb) holds up. Revathi's ghost matches her sheet and the ch20-28 row: indigo and gold sari, jasmine braid, grey threads, sandalwood line, coin necklace with a tali-like pendant, gold armlet. The clay lamp, ink pot and stylus match the archive room. v01 was not offered as a candidate; it shows Ramayyan's face in what should be a hands-only insert.

Clean. The leaf lies flat on the table, square to camera, with exactly three empty bands for the three LEAF lines. The lamp at right rakes across the leaf. Ramayyan's ink-stained hand (five sound digits, white sleeve, no face) rests at the left edge beside the binding. The clay tags are blank. No ghosted face. The archive room matches the neighbouring panels.

Acceptable, with small continuity notes. The leaf reads as held up against the archive room rather than lying flat on the table as in 3.3. The background lamp is a brass bowl, while 3.2 and 3.5 use a clay lamp. Ramayyan's ink-nailed thumb sits at the left end, centred on the upper band, and overlaps the start of both bands up to about x=0.17, so the lettering should start at about x=0.18. The two ruled bands are clean: the upper band runs from about y=0.42 to 0.58 and the lower from about y=0.58 to 0.75. The two short ink strokes sit low in the lower band's right-hand third (x about 0.69 to 0.85), as the script asks, so 'before next monsoon' can be set over them. Partial fingers above and below the leaf at the left edge read as a grip. There are no outlined boxes and no text, and the clay tags carry only abstract dots and slots. v01 was not offered; it has painted outlined boxes.

Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch21 row: high topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, small gold ear stud, silver chain, cream shoulder cloth, and no knife, bandages or coat. His eyes are lowered to the leaf. There is faint stipple shading on the chin and jaw, but no beard; it reads as clean-shaven at page size. Ramayyan's ink-stained right hand comes in from frame right in a white sleeve, and the anatomy is sound. He presses down a tied bundle at the bottom of the frame rather than turning over a single leaf, but the act of hiding the leaf still reads. The setting matches the page: archive shelves, abstract clay tags, a high narrow window and a clay lamp. Both captions have room in the low-detail stone wall at upper right (x 0.70 to 0.97, y 0.0 to 0.5) and over the shelves at upper left (x 0.0 to 0.25), away from the face and hand.

Minor issues, still acceptable. The script implies a finger-on-leaf insert with Ramayyan off panel. Instead he is drawn in a medium shot, face visible, holding the blank leaf up square to camera with his ink-stained fingertip at its left margin. Because he is visible, his line should be lettered as a normal on-panel balloon with its tail pointing to his mouth. His face sits directly above the leaf, so the balloon should go above his head, at top centre over the window, wall and smoke edge, not just above the leaf. The leaf has a single empty band with grain only and no marks. De Lannoy's ghost matches his sheet and the ch16-23 row (pale hair tied back with a black ribbon, white stand-collar tunic-coat, white mundu), but he looks more like he is reading the letter by the flame than burning it. His letter carries faint ruled scribble lines with no letterforms. This is a minor pseudo-writing fault, like the accepted ch12 5.5 leaf. The setting matches the archive room: high barred window, clay lamp with an open wick, ink pot and stylus.

Clean on the beat. Nagoji sits at frame left in the ch21 look: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with only light ink stipple, small flush gold stud, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and no knife, bandages or coat. He wears a half smile that does not reach his eyes. Ramayyan stands at frame right, rising from the low table with one hand on the bundles and one on his knee, and matches his sheet. One minor fault: the brand on Nagoji's left forearm is a small circle with crossed spokes, a wheel-like symbol rather than blurred burned letters. It is tiny at print size, and the long white scar is correct. Ramayyan's head is close to the top edge, so put his long line at top centre over the window and wall, his 'Yes.' at top right over the shelves, and Nagoji's two lines over the shelves at upper left.

Clean. Ramayyan stands alone at frame right, matching his sheet: thin clean-shaven face, receding hairline, plain white cloth, ink-stained fingers. His hand rests on a shelved bundle, a slight sadness shows at the mouth, and he holds a stylus and bundle in the other hand. The clay tags carry double-stroke impressed marks, matching the abstract marks in 1.3, with no script. The plain wall under the high rain-streaked window at upper left leaves ample space for all three balloons, and Nagoji's off-panel tail goes to the left edge. One small spatial oddity: the low table is visible at left with no one at it, even though Nagoji sat beside it in 4.2.

Acceptable with minor continuity faults. On Nagoji, the long forearm scar is pinkish rather than white. A long scar appears on his RIGHT forearm (the arm reaching to the lamp), and the left forearm carries a shorter scar plus a star-shaped brand, so the scar is partly doubled onto the wrong arm. A local paint fix would remove the right-forearm scar. His mundu and shoulder cloth have gold border stripes, unlike the plain mundu in 4.2, though 6.1 also shows a gold border. His jaw shows light stipple stubble, but the chin reads clean-shaven, and the moustache, gold stud, topknot, grey temples and silver chain are all correct. Ramayyan sits at a low shelf at frame right, lifting the cover board off a bundle. He looks down into it rather than angling it toward Nagoji, but the beat reads. The inset at lower right is as scripted: a flat leaf with the board's shadow across its top margin, two empty bands below, and his thumb on the descending board. Letter the two LEAF lines in the middle and bottom bands. The shadow edges into the right end of the upper band, so keep that line left-weighted. Put Nagoji's balloon at upper left, over the window wall or between the heads, and Ramayyan's at upper right over the shelves.

Acceptable. Nagoji is at frame left, standing with his arms crossed and looking away. He has the topknot with grey at the temples, a thick curled moustache, a clean chin (faint shadow only), a gold stud, the silver chain, a plain cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and no knife or coat. Ramayyan is at frame right, composed, hands folded, fingers ink-stained, no chain. The archive room shows rain at the high window and a steady lamp. Minor flag for retouch: the brand on the crossed LEFT forearm is drawn as a small crisp reddish looped mark near the elbow on the outer forearm, not a pale puckered patch above the wrist. At print size it reads as a small mark rather than a letter, but a retoucher could soften it into a pale ridge patch. The shelves over the upper middle and the grey wall above Ramayyan leave room for all three balloons.

Minor only: the lamp is a clay dish on a taller table where 5.1 has a brass lamp on a low table, and the chin carries faint skin-texture shading that still reads as clean-shaven. Character lock is otherwise on-model: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu with the shoulder cloth over the left shoulder as in 5.1, no knife, and the white scar faintly visible on the inner left forearm. He turns toward frame right, where Ramayyan stands off-panel, with a hard, furrowed look. Same archive room and rain-at-the-window lighting as 5.1. The clay tags are blank, and there is no pseudo-text, balloon or box in the art. Both hands are sound. NAGOJI's balloon fits in the low-detail stone wall and window area at upper centre-right. RAMAYYAN (off) fits over the dark background shelves at the right edge.

2026-10-09 regeneration (LEAN-BATCH-195): the same Pune memory as a 3:2 frame with the dark lattice and ceiling across the top third for the three narration balloons (the 3:1 v01 had no place for them that left the executioner's shadow clear). Zones set by Claude from a gridded view; narrator tails run to the top edge (x .3, .7, .7): the three balloons then sit in the lattice band, covering no keep zone.

Acceptable. Ramayyan stands right of centre, head inclined, eyes lowered to the shelf his ink-stained hand rests on, a bundle in his other hand. He matches his sheet (thin face, receding hair, plain white cloth, no chain). Both hands are sound. He is back in the same archive room, with the barred rainy window and the low table. Minor: the lamp is a clay bowl here, where 5.1 and 5.2 show a brass one (both are allowed by the bible, and 5.5 also uses clay). Some clay tags carry simple 'II'-like impressed strokes, which count as abstract marks. The grey corridor wall and the upper-left shelves leave room for both balloons.

Acceptable. Ramayyan has one ink-stained palm flat against a shelf of bundles (hand sound). His sharpened gaze is turned toward frame left, where Nagoji is off-panel, and he matches his sheet. Revathi bleeds in at the right in a blue stain, matching her sheet: indigo-and-gold sari, jasmine braid, gold armlets and bell earrings, a gold necklace with a pendant for the tali, a sandal line and grey at the parting. She raises one palm-out hand against a red-sealed letter held out from beyond the frame by a hand in a dark European cuff. The seal is a plain blob with no lettering. Minor: Ramayyan sits centre-right rather than hard frame right, because Revathi's bleed takes the right edge. The grey wall and window area at upper left and the shelves above his head leave room for both balloons.

Minor only. Both men are on sheet: Nagoji has the topknot, the curled moustache, a clean chin with only faint shading, the gold stud, the silver chain and grey at the temples. Ramayyan is bald-crowned with curly sides, clean-shaven, in white cloth with ink-stained fingers and no chain. Nagoji's brand and white scar are on the correct (left) forearm but sit near the elbow, not a hand's width above the wrist. Ramayyan sits fairly upright, not leaning hard over the table. The table has an extra bench section at the right edge. Lettering space: the dark back wall under and around the high window in the centre, and the shelves above Nagoji at top left. No text in the art; the tags are blank.

Ramayyan's eyes are cast down toward the bundle, so the script's 'knotting the string without looking' is softened. The retying action itself is clear, and the hands are sound and ink-stained. He is on sheet, with the same room, lamp and rainy high window. Lettering space: the plain dark wall right of centre, under and beside the window.

There is a small white scar on Nagoji's near (right) upper arm; the bible puts the scar only on the inner left forearm. It is tiny at this scale. The table reads longer than the low table in 6.1. Otherwise the beat is right: a high angle, Ramayyan standing and sliding the bundle into the wall of tagged bundles, and Nagoji small beside the table, with topknot, moustache, clean chin, stud and chain. Lettering space: the open floor between Nagoji and the table and shelves for the two Ramayyan balloons, and the upper-left wall by the window for the caption.

Minor only. Nagoji is standing at the left with his arms folded, on sheet with a clean chin and the stud. His brand shows faintly on the left forearm near the elbow, as a blank ring with no letters. Ramayyan is at the right, turned back from the shelf toward him with the bundle still in hand. His fingertips are very heavily blackened with ink. Lettering space: the wall and upper shelves between the two heads, around the high window, top centre.

Ramayyan is seated at the table with a stylus again, after standing at the shelf in 6.4, which is a posture jump. A soft-focus cream-clothed shoulder of the other man intrudes at frame left, so he is not fully off-panel; it reads as an over-the-shoulder view of Nagoji, with no face. The inset smile reads gentle and wistful more than a sad twist, though the eye lines show weariness. The inset slightly clips the end of the bundle. Lettering space: the back wall and window column at top left for Ramayyan's long line, the shelves and soft shoulder at the upper left edge for Nagoji's off-panel line, and the cream cloth at the lower left of the inset for the inset line, clear of the face.

Minor only: the Goa brand on Nagoji's left forearm is a small reddish circular stamp with a mark inside, not a pale puckered patch. It is tiny at print size and not legible. The grey at his temples is a little heavier than 'first grey'. Ramayyan sits mid-size at frame right rather than small among the shelves. Otherwise clean: Nagoji at the door at frame left looking back, with topknot, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, silver chain and cream mundu with shoulder cloth. Ramayyan matches his sheet with ink-stained fingers and no chain. Pale drizzle light comes through the high window. The bundle tags are blank. Lettering can sit on the plain back wall around the window and above Ramayyan's head.

Minor only: the lamp sits on a standing-height table, while 7.1 and 7.4 show the low floor table. The brand is again a small dark circular stamp rather than a pale puckered patch, not legible at print size. The tags carry very faint scratch marks that do not show at page scale. Two-shot is correct: Nagoji at frame left squaring up, Ramayyan at frame right unmoved with ink-stained fingers and no chain. The plain grey back wall between them (x 0.43 to 0.65, y 0.03 to 0.40) takes both balloons.

Minor only. Nagoji's forearm reaches further into the frame than 'just in frame at the lower left edge', but it is wrist, hand and shoulder-cloth edge only, with no face. The brand is a pale puckered patch with no letters, and the long white scar is on the inner forearm, both as the bible requires. The hand is sound (thumb and four fingers). Ramayyan matches his sheet, with his eyes dropped to the brand. Light drizzle shows through the window, consistent with 7.1. The two long balloons fit in the dark shelf and wall area at the upper left (x 0 to 0.5, y 0 to 0.3) without covering his face or the wrist.

Minor only. Nagoji is in the background at frame left but drawn sharp rather than soft. His ch21 look checks out: topknot, grey at the temples, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, gold ear stud, silver chain, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, with his hands behind his back so the brand is hidden. Ramayyan has his back to Nagoji and his palm flat on the bundles. His fingers are ink-stained and the hand is sound. The same archive, lamp table and window carry over from 7.1 and 7.2. The plain grey wall between the two men (x 0.32 to 0.52, y 0.15 to 0.65) holds all three balloons.

Minor only. The lean man with the dark maroon cloth over one shoulder is shaded dark against the lamplight but not a full silhouette, and his bearded face is partly readable. He stands straight among the bowed crowd, a couple of steps behind and to the side of the king. Varma matches the varma-v1 face: dark hair bound back, no crown or turban, bare-chested, plain mundu, gold necklaces. He sweeps with a coconut-leaf broom and both hands grip it soundly. The women setting lamp rows, the small priests (backs turned) and the stain-edged warm border all match the script. There is no painted text. The two captions sit in the dusk sky and roof band along the top (x 0.36 to 0.62, y 0 to 0.15) or the top-left roof corner.

Acceptable; the v01 problems are fixed. The frame holds only hands, forearms and the knife, with no face on either man. The assassin's arm enters from frame left with the dark shoulder cloth from 7.5. The defender's bare forearm enters from the bottom edge, attached to no body, and clamps the knife wrist. It carries a pale, raised, ridged brand, unreadable and not a cross, with the long white scar beside it. The dagger point stops at the king's bare side at frame right. There is no blood, no chain and no painted text, and the stain-edged border and warm lamp palette match 7.5. Small points: the king's mundu shows gold kasavu stripes, while 7.5 v02 has a plain mundu. The knife pommel shows as a brass ring just past the defender's fingers and reads a little like a bracelet. The brand's ridges form a knot-like shape rather than a shapeless patch, but they can't be read. The panel has no lettering.

Acceptable. The r2 failures are fixed. The stain-edged parchment memory border now runs round all four edges, matching 7.5 and 8.1. Varma has jet-black hair bound back with no grey, no necklaces and a plain cream mundu, and he is bare-chested and bare-headed. Every script beat is present: a high, distant aftermath; two forms under gold-bordered temple cloth; broken clay pots; scattered flowers; golden spilled oil (no blood); the dropped knife lower right; the broom lying in the oil; three kneeling Nair guards with round shields and curved swords; Varma sitting up with a hand to his head; and a bare-backed third man vanishing into the crowd at upper right. Hands and anatomy are sound, and nothing is painted as text. Minor points: the guards' topknots sit on the crown or back of the head rather than forward, and Varma's mundu hem shows a faint gold edge. For the letterer: the open night sky is only a narrow strip (about x 0.27 to 0.80, y 0.02 to 0.10). The long caption should sit there and may spill onto the dark tiled roofs (up to y 0.17). Keep it above the shrine figures and the crowd heads, which start near y 0.20.

Acceptable. The r2 failures are fixed. The ear carries a tiny flush gold stud on the lobe with nothing hanging. The chin and jaw are smooth and clean-shaven under a thick curled moustache, with only hair at the sideburn. The forearm across his stomach shows no mark of any kind (no cross, no brand visible), and the hand gripping the cloth is well formed. He has the Kerala topknot (with a thin gold hair tie), first grey at the temple, a silver chain, and the cream mundu with shoulder cloth. There is no knife, coat or bandage. Nagoji lies alone on his back on the stone platform against the jackfruit trunk, eyes open. A single raindrop hangs from a leaf at about x 0.47, y 0.14. The dry courtyard, the lit house at left, the kalari pavilion with wooden weapon racks at right and the palms with a sea glint beyond the wall all match 8.5 v01, including the arm-behind-head pose. Nothing is painted as text. Captions: the starry sky upper right (about x 0.52 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.30) is low in detail and holds all three stacked captions, clear of the face and the drop.

Acceptable. The v01 anachronism is fixed: the clerk now writes with a plain feather quill whose own shaft is cut to an ink-darkened point, with no steel nib or collar. The split holds both halves. On the left, in cold grey light, are the dark-cuffed, lace-edged clerk's hand, the quill and the blank ruled ledger. On the right, in warm lamp light, are Ramayyan's ink-stained fingers, the stylus and the flat palm leaf, with his plain white cloth, no jewellery and no faces. Nothing is painted as text. The LEDGER line fits on the empty ruled lines of the left page, near the quill tip, at about x 0.08 to 0.42, y 0.45 to 0.65. The LEAF line fits on the top face of the leaf, either left of the stylus tip (x 0.54 to 0.68) or right of it (x 0.71 to 0.90), at y 0.55 to 0.61. That band is narrow, so the incised face will need to be small. Room for the captions: the plain grey wall at top left (x 0.22 to 0.45, y 0.01 to 0.16) and the brown wall at top left of the right half or the plain table at right (x 0.71 to 1.0, y 0.67 to 0.80). Minor points: the leaf's grain reads as several faint bands rather than one. Ramayyan's resting left fingertips just overlap the leaf's far top-right edge, though they do not cover the lettering area. The left half is not an exact recomposition of chapter 1 panel 1.2: that panel has a red cuff with the hand entering from the right. The script itself asks for a dark cuff and grey light here.

Acceptable. It matches the script: a high pull-back over the courtyard, the jackfruit tree, Nagoji small and reclining on the stone platform, consistent with his pose in 8.3. He has his topknot, moustache, clean chin, cream mundu and shoulder cloth, and a faint silver chain. Stars overhead, and a storm bank with silent lightning glowing over the sea on the far right horizon. Caveats for the letterer: the clear sky is only a narrow strip above the palms (about x 0.50 to 0.78, y 0 to 0.15) because the canopy fills the top centre. The four captions will need to stack there and spill onto the dark treeline and the open courtyard ground at lower right (about x 0.56 to 0.72, y 0.62 to 0.95), keeping clear of the storm glow at upper right and of Nagoji. Minor: one lamp-lit verandah at left makes the estate less than fully dark, and a tiny pale mark on his upper arm is invisible at print size.
